## Growth Rate by Temperature and Population

```{r}
df.t <- read.csv('/Users/mcdonaldlab1/Desktop/R/R_week3/tempExperiment_v2.csv')

df.t$temp <- factor(df.t$temp)

boxplot(df.t$growthRate ~ df.t$temp + df.t$pop,
        names = c('10', '20', '10', '20'),
        at = c(1, 2, 4, 5),
        ylab = 'Growth rate mm/day',
        xlab = '')

mtext('Pop 1', side = 1, at = 1.5, line = 3)
mtext('Pop 2', side = 1, at = 4.5, line = 3)
```

## ANOVA Results

```{r}
m1.summary <- readRDS('/Users/mcdonaldlab1/Desktop/R/R_week3/m1.summary.rds')

m1.summary
```

## Interpretation

The ANOVA results show that temperature, population, and the interaction between temperature and population were not statistically significant at the 0.05 level. Temperature had a p-value of 0.0798, population had a p-value of 0.2379, and the interaction had a p-value of 0.5974.
